witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaign sets ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raises it. The observed maximum is 310,957 on CommitFailure/head-vacant.

A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. Before 2026-09-01 this campaign measured NOTHING, which is why the next witness is a first observation rather than a regression guard.

Capture was 1,255 bytes as a legacy message and Settle 1,321, against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES -- over by 23 and 89, so neither could be submitted anywhere and ProgramTest submits no packet to say so. Both classes now execute as v0 messages over a table frozen for that class, built before the campaign starts driving the Clock by hand because create_lookup_table needs a slot the bank actually produced. 29 and 31 of the frame's addresses become one-byte indexes; three stay static in each -- the payer, the invoked program, and the worker, who signs. One line per class rather than a max, so a single class drifting cannot hide behind another.

Against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES. Eight transactions -- four Capture and four Settle -- were over it before 2026-09-02. Nulls are excluded on purpose: an unmeasured transaction is not a transaction that fits, and `sponsored-measured-every-transaction` is what holds that count at zero.

CommitFailure is 1,222 bytes on a legacy message, ten under Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES, and it is now the widest transaction this campaign submits. It stays legacy DELIBERATELY, and the ten bytes are the reason to keep watching it: one more account, or the twelve-byte priority-fee instruction the house builder pushes unconditionally, puts it over -- and a FAILURE route is the last one that should acquire a published lookup table as a liveness precondition. If it grows, the answer is to shrink its frame, not to give it a table.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error == null) | .label | split("/")[0]] | unique | sort | join(" + ")
witnesses.provenance: SponsoredPushActionV1 has exactly five variants (crates/dclutch-source/src/resolution/sponsored_push_v1.rs), and process_sponsored_push_v1 dispatches one arm per variant. This asserts that every one of the five is observed EXECUTING, not merely refusing -- a family whose actions are only ever seen red is a family with no evidence that it works.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | .logs[] | select(test("failed: custom program error")) | capture("0x(?<c>[0-9a-f]+)").c] | unique | sort | join(",")
witnesses.provenance: The nine hostiles do not share one code. Read off the fold rather than off the enum: 0x8009 ProviderRelease, 0x800c Transition, 0x800e Funding, 0x8012 ProviderFreshness, 0x8015 SponsoredPush -- all in Resolution's registered band 8 (crates/dclutch-refusal-registry). This witness exists because the census lane's own draft failed exactly here: six hostiles sharing one label had the first one's code written for all of them, and five raised something else.
